h1:
First Time in Pattaya
What You Need to Know
intro: Pattaya sits just about 2 hours from Bangkok, making it the easiest beach trip for anyone in the capital or flying into Suvarnabhumi. If it's your first time, you might be unsure where to stay, how to get around town, or where to catch the boat to Koh Larn. We've pulled together everything worth knowing before you go, plus a 2-day plan you can actually follow.

blocks.html: Pattaya has changed a lot from its old reputation. These days you'll find quiet stretches like Jomtien Beach, the clear water of Koh Larn, hillside cafes, sunset viewpoints, and reasonably priced seafood. At the same time there's still a lively late-night entertainment scene, so it's a city you can do several ways in one trip. This guide answers the common first-timer questions before walking you through a plan.

blocks.text: How to get from Bangkok to Pattaya

blocks.html: Pattaya is about 150 km from Bangkok, roughly a 2-hour drive (closer to 3 hours on holidays). Here are the main options.

items: Van / minibus from Ekkamai — leaves from Ekkamai bus terminal and drops you in Central Pattaya. Tickets run around 140–160 THB, with frequent departures from morning to evening. Good if you don't have a car.

Bus from Mo Chit / Suvarnabhumi — several operators, with tickets starting around 130–160 THB. From Suvarnabhumi Airport, Bell Travel runs straight to Pattaya hotels for about 140 THB, taking 1.5–2 hours.
Driving yourself — Motorway 7 is the easiest route if you're with a group or family. Parking is available at hotels and malls.
Taxi / private car with driver — comfortable but pricey, best when there are a few of you to split the cost.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: On Friday evenings or long weekends, traffic leaving Bangkok gets heavy. Add at least an hour of buffer, or leave before 2 pm for a smoother run.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Pattaya trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

blocks.text: Where to stay as a first-timer

blocks.html: Pattaya stretches along the coast, and each area has its own feel. Pick based on the kind of trip you want.

items.name: Central Pattaya
items.blurb: Right in the middle and the most convenient to get around, close to Central mall, restaurants, and easy connections elsewhere. Good for first-timers still finding their feet.

items.name: Jomtien Beach
items.blurb: A longer, quieter beach that suits families and anyone who really wants to relax. Has a night market and beachfront seafood spots.

items.name: Naklua / Wongamat
items.blurb: North of town, quieter and more local, near Naklua fish market. Good for seafood lovers and a less crowded vibe.

items.name: South Pattaya / Walking Street
items.blurb: The nightlife hub, buzzing until late and great for partygoers. If you're after a quiet break, skip this zone.

blocks.html: Room prices swing clearly with the season and holidays. On weekdays in the off-season you can land a nice room at an easy price, but long weekends and high season (Nov–Feb) push rates up and fill fast. Book ahead.

blocks.text: Getting around Pattaya — songthaews, motorbikes, taxis

items: Songthaew (baht bus) — runs a fixed loop along Beach Road and Pattaya 2nd Road. Just hop on and press the buzzer to get off. Fares start at 15 THB per person for in-town rides; going as far as Jomtien or Naklua may be 20 THB.
Chartering a songthaew — if you want to go somewhere off the loop, agree on the price before you get in every time, or you'll get quoted high.
Motorbike taxi — fastest if you're solo. Again, agree on the fare first.
Ride-hailing apps (Grab / Bolt) — work in Pattaya, with clear prices and no haggling. Handy at night or with luggage.
Renting a motorbike — 200–300 THB a day and great for freedom, but you need a license, wear a helmet, and watch the traffic on Beach Road.

blocks.title: Watch the price
blocks.html: Songthaews parked and waiting for charter passengers tend to quote high. To pay the normal rate, flag one already doing its loop and pay when you get off. For a charter, always confirm the price clearly before you climb in.

items.name: Koh Larn
items.blurb: A clear-water island about 7 km offshore with several beaches to choose from — lively Tawaen Beach and the quieter Tien Beach. Swim, snorkel, or laze on the sand all day. Take the ferry from Bali Hai Pier.
items.meta: Full day · Ferry 40 THB/trip · Speedboat around 150–200 THB

items.name: Sanctuary of Truth
items.blurb: An entirely hand-carved wooden temple by the sea in Naklua, still under construction after more than 40 years. The woodwork is remarkably detailed, and there's a guided tour of about 30 minutes.

items.name: Khao Chi Chan (Buddha Mountain)
items.blurb: A huge laser-etched Buddha image on a cliff face, visible from a distance. It's south of Pattaya and pairs nicely with Nong Nooch Garden.

items.name: Pratamnak Hill Viewpoint
items.blurb: Looks out over the whole of Pattaya Bay, lovely by day and at sunset. There's a Pattaya sign for photos up top, and it's an easy trip from the city center.

items.name: Nong Nooch Garden
items.blurb: A large botanical garden with a French garden, a dinosaur valley, and cultural shows. Good for families and anyone who likes taking photos. It's out of town to the south.

items.name: Wihan Sien / Big Buddha at Khao Phra Bat
items.blurb: A spot to pay respects and take in the city from above. The Big Buddha on Khao Phra Bat is close to town and easy to reach — a good evening stop.

items.name: Tiffany's Cabaret Show
items.blurb: Pattaya's long-running cabaret with elaborate costumes. A nice evening outing before heading back to your hotel. Booking tickets ahead usually gets a better price.

items.name: Art in Paradise (3D Art Museum)
items.blurb: A 3D painting museum that's fun for photos, fully indoors. Good for a rainy day or with kids, and it's in the city center.

blocks.html: This plan is built to be doable as written: day one stays on land near town, day two heads out to the island. Scale it up or down to your energy.

items.activity: Travel from Bangkok to Pattaya, check in, and drop your bags.
items.note: Leaving Bangkok early gives you a full day to explore.

items.activity: Visit the Sanctuary of Truth in Naklua, walk the carved woodwork and join the guided tour.
items.note: Entry is around 500 THB. Dress modestly; there are lovely seaside photo spots.

items.activity: Lunch around Naklua — try the seafood at Naklua fish market.
items.note: Prices go by weight, so ask before you order to be sure.

items.activity: Rest at your hotel, or stop by Art in Paradise if the sun's strong or it's raining.
items.note: The afternoon sun is harsh, so an indoor option works well.

items.activity: Head up to Pratamnak Hill Viewpoint for sunset and a photo at the Pattaya sign.
items.note: Arrive about an hour before sunset for the best light.

items.activity: Wander Jomtien Night Market for street food and souvenirs.
items.note: Open roughly 5–11 pm, with plenty of food at friendly prices.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Koh Larn, a full day in the water

items.activity: Go to Bali Hai Pier and catch the ferry to Koh Larn.
items.note: Ferry is around 40 THB/trip on set departures, so arrive ahead of time.

items.activity: Pick a beach on the island — swim, snorkel, or rent a deck chair and settle in.
items.note: Tawaen Beach is lively; Tien and Samae beaches are quieter.

items.activity: Lunch on seafood by the beach, then shelter from the midday sun.
items.note: Prices on the island run a touch higher than the mainland, which is normal.

items.activity: Take the boat back, pack up, and leave buffer for the trip back to Bangkok.
items.note: The last boat back is around 6 pm — don't miss it.

blocks.title: About the boat to the island
blocks.html: Always check the weather before heading out. If the wind and waves pick up or there's a warning, postpone or switch to a land-based day instead. Safety first — and don't forget your life jacket on a speedboat.

blocks.text: If you only have one day, how to make Pattaya count

blocks.label: Day trip
blocks.title: Bangkok and back in a day

items.activity: Leave Bangkok early, and on arrival head straight to Bali Hai Pier for Koh Larn.
items.note: With one day, pick one — the island or the city.

items.activity: Spend half a day in the water at Koh Larn and have seafood by the beach.
items.note: If you'd rather skip the island, swap in the Sanctuary of Truth + Pratamnak Hill.

items.activity: Take the boat back, then stop at Pratamnak Hill Viewpoint or pick up souvenirs.
items.note: Leave buffer for the drive back — holiday evenings get jammed.
Leaving before the rush-hour exodus helps you dodge motorway traffic.

blocks.html: Pattaya has a lively late-night scene, especially Walking Street in South Pattaya. If you're heading out at night, going out with your wits about you and looking after yourself matters.

items: Ask the price before ordering — some bars add service charges or have unlisted prices, so check the bill every time before paying.
Mind your valuables — carry only the cash you need and keep your phone, wallet, and passport secure. Watch your bag in crowds.
Don't accept drinks from strangers — and don't leave your glass unattended.
Get back with a ride you trust — late at night, Grab or Bolt is safer and the price is set.
Drink in moderation — keep an eye on your group so everyone makes it back.

blocks.text: Other things worth knowing before you go

items: Best time to visit — Nov–Feb has good weather and clear water but draws crowds and higher prices · Mar–May is hot but quieter · the rainy season needs an indoor backup plan.
Cash — small shops, markets, and boat fares run on cash, so keep small notes on hand.
Strong sun — wear sunscreen and bring a hat and water, especially on island days.
Temple dress code — the Sanctuary of Truth and temples expect modest dress covering shoulders and knees.
Bargaining for tours / water activities — beach prices swing with the season and holidays, so ask a few vendors and compare before paying.

blocks.title: First-timer summary
blocks.html: Stay in Central Pattaya or Jomtien on your first trip, use the songthaew and pay on exit for in-town hops, set aside a day for Koh Larn and a half day in the city, check the weather before any boat, and look after your valuables at night. Do that and your first trip runs smoothly.

faq.q: Where should I stay in Pattaya for the first time?
faq.a: For a first visit, Central Pattaya is the easiest pick — most convenient to get around, close to malls, and simple to connect onward. If you want quiet and a family feel, choose Jomtien Beach. Partygoers should look around South Pattaya near Walking Street, but if you're after a relaxing break, skip that zone.

faq.q: How much is the boat to Koh Larn?
faq.a: The ferry from Bali Hai Pier to Koh Larn is around 40 THB per trip (up from 30 THB as of April 2026), running on set departures, with the last boat back around 6 pm. A speedboat is faster but pricier at roughly 150–200 THB per person. Always check the weather before heading out.

faq.q: How do songthaews work in Pattaya, and what do they cost?
faq.a: The blue songthaews run a fixed loop along Beach Road and Pattaya 2nd Road. Just hop on and press the buzzer to get off. Fares start at 15 THB per person for in-town rides; going as far as Jomtien or Naklua may be 20 THB. To go somewhere off the loop you'll need to agree on a charter price before getting in every time.

faq.q: How much is entry to the Sanctuary of Truth?
faq.a: Adult entry is around 500 THB, with a lower rate for children, and it includes a guided tour of the structure. It's open daily. Dress modestly as it's a cultural site. Prices may change, so it's worth confirming on the day.

faq.q: Is one day enough for Pattaya?
faq.a: It's enough for a taster. Pick one — half a day swimming at Koh Larn, or in-town sights like the Sanctuary of Truth and Pratamnak Hill Viewpoint. But if you want both the beach and the city without rushing, 2 days and 1 night works out better.
